To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) lazy replication protocols, which have been used for many years to provide scalability and availability, are not durable, and (2) our approach of using "buddy replicas" to provide durability for lazy replication protocols is efficient, easy to implement, and provides a good balance between efficiency and durability.

(i) the buddy system can be used to provide durability for Web Service Transactions in the presence of failures, (ii) our approach requires only two synchronous updates, and (iii) the buddy selection algorithm ensures correct execution, and can be easily adapted for workload balancing.
the lazy replica update propagation protocol, which is used to reduce latency and improve efficiency, can be made durable by synchronizing updates in two replicas, which we call buddies.

the cost of increased transaction correctness and durability in the context of Web Services.
the problem of how to provide durability for Web Service transactional updates in a cost-effective way.
the problem of providing high levels of durability in the presence of failures in a Web Service environment.

the lazy replica update propagation approach, which is widely used in practice, is vulnerable to data loss in the presence of server crashes.
